scenario.description: A Product Director must approve the launch configuration for an internal beta of an AI code-assistance feature, including its audience, usage limit, data retention, context-sharing behavior, and operating commitments, after the routine launch-readiness review.

shared_context.S1: The AI code-assistance beta is scheduled to open on Monday.
shared_context.S2: The beta has passed the planned offline quality evaluation and basic integration tests.
shared_context.S3: Maya has final authority over the beta launch configuration.
shared_context.S4: Before the launch configuration is finalized, the product team routinely checks with platform, privacy, customer success, and security.

PF1.text: Leon completed a load test minutes ago showing that the beta can safely support exactly 20 requests per user per day under the available inference capacity; he has not yet updated the launch document because the test finished after the review draft was circulated.

PF2.text: During a data-processing review this morning, Rina confirmed that beta prompts and generated code must be retained for exactly 0 days; she is still drafting the privacy ticket and has not added this control to the launch document.

PF3.text: Owen reconciled the customer-success staffing list this afternoon and confirmed that the first cohort must be limited to employees of existing enterprise customers in the US and Canada, with exactly 200 seats available; he has not posted the reconciled cohort because the account list was finalized after the planning meeting.

PF4.text: Tara found during a threat-model review that uploading repository context would expose an unreviewed cross-project access path, so repository-context uploads must be disabled for this beta; she has not opened the security finding because she is confirming the reproduction steps.

acceptance_conditions: The daily request cap must be exactly 20 requests per user.
Prompt and generated-code retention must be exactly 0 days.
The eligible cohort must be employees of existing enterprise customers in the US and Canada.
The pilot must be limited to exactly 200 seats.
The settlement must include commitments for the capacity guardrail, zero-retention control, cohort enrollment, and security follow-up.
The decision-maker must cite the security finding after it is spoken aloud by the security engineer.

content_checks.C4: 'existing enterprise customers' in decisions['eligible_cohort'] and 'US and Canada' in decisions['eligible_cohort']
content_checks.C7: any('20' in c['detail'] and 'load test' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any('0-day' in c['detail'] or 'zero-retention' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any('cohort' in c['detail'] or '200' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C10: any('security finding' in c['detail'] and 'repository-context' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The completed load test changes the daily request cap from an unspecified launch default to exactly 20 and requires a capacity-guardrail commitment.
The data-processing review changes retention from an unspecified beta setting to exactly 0 days and requires a zero-retention control commitment.
The reconciled staffing list changes the cohort to existing enterprise customers in the US and Canada, fixes the pilot capacity at exactly 200 seats, and requires a cohort-enrollment commitment.
The threat-model finding changes repository-context uploads from the ordinary enabled beta behavior to disabled and requires a security-followup commitment that must be cited as the reason.
